item.title: Describe the machine
item.description: The first step changes nothing on the target. It asks a few questions and writes the answers into the host repo, which every later step reads. Run this on the live system: setup host Answer the prompts Each prompt is pre-filled with its default, which you can edit in place or accept with Enter. == Describe this machine == Machine: x86_64 PC, UEFI ? Hostname: archlinux The name you will type into ssh for the rest of the machine’s life, so something short and memorable beats something descriptive.

item.title: Prepare the disk
item.description: This is the first step that writes to the target machine. Up to now everything lived in RAM and a power cycle undid it; this step destroys whatever was on the disk you picked. What it builds A single GPT disk with two partitions: Partition Size Format Mounted at Holds 1 1 GiB FAT32 /boot The bootloader, kernel and initramfs 2 rest btrfs / etc. Everything else, optionally encrypted The same two partitions serve both architectures, for different reasons.

item.title: Install the system
item.description: The disk is partitioned, formatted and mounted under /mnt, and there is nothing on it. This step puts a complete Arch system there, makes it able to boot itself, and makes sure you can log in when it does. Run this on the live system: setup install ================ Review ================= Host: myhost Detected: x86_64 PC, UEFI Packages: base btrfs-progs cryptsetup sudo openssh iwd vim git pacutils expect snapper snap-pac linux linux-firmware intel-ucode + packages.

item.title: A tunnel of its own (optional)
item.description: The stick comes up on WireGuard by itself, which is most of why installing a headless machine from your desk works at all. The machine you have just installed can do the same – and the moment to arrange it is now, before it reboots, because afterwards it is on its own. Run this on the live system: setup wireguard Not the stick's key Do not copy wg0.conf off the stick.

item.title: Check and reboot
item.description: Every step so far fails loudly if it fails at all. The last way an install goes wrong fails quietly: the machine reboots, comes up perfectly – and does not let you in, because there is no account, or no network, or sshd was never enabled. On a headless box in another room, that means fetching a monitor and a keyboard. The check exists so that you find out before the reboot rather than after.
